name: desire for food
description: Physical or mental desire to eat.
perceptions: Physical hunger or clock says it's time to eat.

guidance.description: Dieting and breaking diets is common. You know whether it's time to seek help.

variations.name: biological hunger
variations.description: Hunger is an uncomfortably empty feeling in the belly driving you to seek nourishment.

variations.name: clock says hungry
variations.description: Often in the modern world, we're ready to eat mostly because the clock says it's time for a meal and you're ready for a break from work. Often these breaks are cherished parts of the day.
perceptions: Not necessarily hungry, but it's time to eat.

variations.name: grazing
variations.description: You can feel a desire for food by watching others eat. For example, watching an advertisement that shows happy people eating your favorite dish.
perceptions: Others are eating, that looks enjoyable. I should join them.

variations.name: comfort snacking
variations.description: Snacking can be driven by a deep desire for comfort brought about by the sensations and brain chemicals of eating, and of having the economic luxury to do so.
perceptions: It would be nice to have a snack and there's no harm in doing so.

commentaries.quote: It may be helpful to be aware of why you're heading to the refrigerator: boredom, anxiety, social bonding, or actual hunger.
Food is a lot of people's therapy - when we say comfort food, we really mean that. It's releasing dopamine and serotonin in your brain that makes you feel good.
A party without cake is just a meeting.
Food is our common ground, a universal experience
